docs.title: Alcatel-Lucent: HA switching, built in the UI and in code
docs.text:
Welcome, and thank you for joining us. Today you tour a live, highly available Alcatel-Lucent OmniSwitch fabric, see how it was built by hand and how the same build is written as code, and see how a lab runs that fabric as code every day, without anyone touching it by hand.

Begin: Lab 0 Read the student guide

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1 · Get your login

Your instructor gives you one username and password. It opens everything in this class.

2 · Read the student guide

The student guide explains how the class works and lists the labs in order, with their times.

3 · Do Lab 0

Lab 0 takes about 10 minutes: sign in everywhere and check your tools.

docs.title: What you will do
docs.text:
• Read the health of a two-chassis OmniSwitch Virtual Chassis: who is master, whether the stack links are up, whether both chassis agree
  • Follow each HA build step twice: at the console, then as code that a pipeline applies and checks
  • See how a fabric is run as code: plan, apply, read-back, drift, and why nothing is ever changed by hand
  • (coming soon) Review the same switches in OmniVista Cirrus, ALE's cloud management service, signed in with your Microsoft account

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A web browser. That is all: every lab is read-only, and the instructor drives the live switch on screen. The command cheat sheet is optional.
  • Your login from the instructor. This site never contains passwords, and you never need to type one into it.

docs.text:

This class is designed and delivered by Paragon Micro, in the Paragon Micro lab. Who we are →

  • Your login doesn't work: your instructor can reset it. Don't keep retrying: three wrong tries locks the account for a while.

This site is public and never contains passwords or anything about your company's environment.

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text: A data centre switch pair has two jobs: carry traffic, and keep carrying it when one switch fails. Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise (ALE) does this with a Virtual Chassis: two OmniSwitches joined by stack links that act as one switch with one configuration. You will read that kind of fabric while it carries real traffic, follow how it was built, once by hand and once as code, and see how it is run day to day: nothing is changed by hand, and every change is planned, applied by a pipeline and read back before it is saved.

docs.title: Your login, and what you need
docs.text:
Everything in this class is read-only. The switch you study is a working production fabric in the Paragon Micro lab, so:

Resource How you see it The live switch your instructor shows it on screen, read-only Its state at the start of class your instructor shows this booking's snapshot, captured read-only when the class was set up The code that builds and runs it shown on screen and on these pages OmniVista Cirrus (coming soon) your class login, through Microsoft sign-in, as a Viewer

You never type a password into this site, and this site never shows one.

docs.title: How the lab is put together
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph VC["Virtual Chassis: one logical switch"]
    C1["Chassis 1<br/>(master)"] <== "2 x 100G stack links (VFL)" ==> C2["Chassis 2<br/>(slave)"]
  end
  S1["Server"] -- "LACP leg 1" --> C1
  S1 -- "LACP leg 2" --> C2
  Git["Code in git"] -- "plan / apply / read back" --> VC
  Cirrus["OmniVista Cirrus (coming soon)"] -. "read-only view" .-> VC

Every server connects with one cable to each chassis, bundled with LACP. Lose a cable, a chassis or a stack link, and every server still has a path.

docs.text:
Before class, a pipeline signed in to the live switch read-only, ran a fixed list of show commands, and saved the output as this booking's snapshot. Your instructor shows it on screen. Nothing in this class changes the live switch. Lab diagram.

docs.title: 0.3 Learn to read a command line
docs.text:
show virtual-chassis topology
^^^^ ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ^^^^^^^^
verb feature         what about it

docs.title: Lab 1: Tour a live HA fabric
docs.text: Version 0.2.0 · draft · 2026-11-18 · class/guides/01-tour-the-fabric.md

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
How to read the health of a two-chassis OmniSwitch Virtual Chassis (VC): which chassis is master, whether the stack links are up, whether both chassis agree, and how servers attach to both. Then you work out what each failure would cost.

Time: 25 minutes · Before you start: Lab 0 done

docs.title: How the lab is set up for this lab
docs.text:
The live VC is two OmniSwitch 6900 chassis with two 100G stack links, carrying a working lab's servers and storage. Your instructor shows this booking's snapshot. The outputs below are trimmed examples. Lab diagram.

Your browser does not play this video.

🎬 Lab 1: tour a live HA fabric. Watch it, then follow the same steps below.

docs.title: 1.1 Who is in charge?
docs.text:
show virtual-chassis topology

Chas  Role     Status
----+--------+---------
 1    Master   Running
 2    Slave    Running

One chassis is master (it runs the control plane). The other is slave, ready to take over. A configured priority picks the master, so the result is the same after every reboot.

docs.title: 1.2 Are the stack links up?
docs.text: show virtual-chassis vf-link. The VFL (virtual fabric link) joins the chassis: two 100G ports per chassis, bundled. With one port down, the VC stays whole.

docs.title: 1.3 Do both chassis agree?
docs.text: show virtual-chassis consistency: same software, same chassis group, same control VLAN. Inconsistent means the second chassis will not join.

docs.title: 1.4 How do servers attach?
docs.text: show linkagg and show linkagg port. Each server bond has one port on chassis 1 (1/1/x) and one on chassis 2 (2/1/x), bundled with LACP. Port names are chassis/slot/port.

docs.title: 1.5 Is it saved, and can it roll back?
docs.text:
show running-directory: the switch runs from WORKING. CERTIFIED is the known-good copy it can roll back to.

Think about it

The master chassis loses power. What happens to the servers' traffic, to the management address, and to the configuration? (The slave becomes master. Each server keeps its leg on the surviving chassis. The VC-wide management address follows the new master.)

Done when

You can point at the master, the stack links and one server's two legs, and say what each failure would cost.

docs.title: Thank you
docs.text: Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise: OmniSwitch 6900: Virtual Chassis is described in the datasheet (PDF).

docs.title: Bonus
docs.text: Find a server bond in show linkagg port whose two legs are on the same chassis. (There should be none. Why would one be a problem?)

docs.title: Lab 2: Build it by hand, then as code
docs.text: Version 0.2.0 · draft · 2026-11-18 · class/guides/02-ui-versus-code.md

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
Each step of building an HA pair, done two ways: typed at the console or clicked in the web UI (WebView), and declared once as code that a pipeline applies and checks. You will see why the lab uses the second.

Time: 40 minutes · Before you start: Lab 1 done

docs.title: How the lab is set up for this lab
docs.text:
Sandbox pair (coming soon): you do each step by hand, then the instructor applies the same steps as code. Until then: the instructor walks the steps on screen, and Lab S has every command, the code, and ALE's documentation.

Your browser does not play this video.

🎬 Lab 2: build it by hand, then as code. Watch it, then follow the same steps below.

docs.title: 2.1 The steps, side by side
docs.text: Step By hand (console or WebView) As code (declared once, applied by a pipeline) Lab S Factory safety disable Auto-Fabric and the cloud agent a check after every run: Auto-fabric Status : Disable S.1 Chassis identity + master configured-chassis-id 2 on the second box; priorities 200 / 100 written once, applied by a logged bootstrap S.2 Stack links virtual-chassis auto-vf-link-port 1/1/55 and …/56 checks: both chassis Running, both VFLs Up S.2 Management per-chassis + VC-wide addresses the same values in one file S.3 Accounts user … read-only all passwords in a vault, never in code S.4 VLANs vlan 50 admin-state enable name "…" vlans: {50: …} S.5 Server bonds linkagg lacp agg 1 size 2 … + one port per chassis { id: 1, ports: [1/1/1, 2/1/1] } S.6 Save write memory flash-synchro saved only after a read-back proves every line S.7

docs.title: 2.2 Three things to notice
docs.text:
1. The code is shorter than the typing. One line declares a bond; the pipeline works out the commands.
  2. The code checks itself. On this fabric's first run, the read-back found a mismatch (the switch prints vlan 70-72, the code listed 70, 71, 72) and saved nothing. The fix went into the code, not onto the switch.
  3. The switch refused some commands (a bond number above 127). The fix was to renumber the bonds in the code, once.

Done when

You can explain why "saved only after the read-back" matters more than how quickly a change was made.

docs.title: Thank you
docs.text: The sample declaration and the read-only client are in the Toolkit. ALE: OmniSwitch 6900.

docs.title: Bonus
docs.text: In vc-pair.example.yml, add a third server bond. Which two ports do you choose, and why?

docs.title: Lab 3: Run the fabric as code
docs.text: Version 0.2.0 · draft · 2026-11-18 · class/guides/03-fabric-as-code.md

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
The loop the lab uses for every switch: plan, apply, read back, catch drift. You follow one change through it, see a hand change caught the next morning, and read the performance and hardware data the same tooling collects.

Time: 30 minutes · Before you start: Lab 2 done

docs.title: How the lab is set up for this lab
docs.text:
The live fabric is managed by a pipeline in the lab's network repository. The instructor shows its runs: a plan, an apply, a daily drift plan. The pipeline shape is in fabric-as-code.example.yml. Lab diagram.

Your browser does not play this video.

🎬 Lab 3: run the fabric as code. Watch it, then follow the same steps below.

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  A["Change the file<br/>in git"] --> B["PLAN<br/>(what would change)"]
  B --> C{"Reviewed?"}
  C -- yes --> D["APPLY<br/>backup, send, read back, save"]
  D --> E["PLAN again<br/>must say 0 changes"]
  F["Every day"] --> G["PLAN<br/>red if the switch differs"]

docs.title: 3.1 Plan
docs.text: A run that only plans: the lines it would send, and nothing sent.

docs.title: 3.2 Apply
docs.text: The run backs up the configuration, sends only the missing lines, reads every line back, then saves. If the read-back fails, nothing is saved, and the backup is still the last good copy.

docs.title: 3.3 Prove it is idempotent
docs.text: Run the plan again. It must report 0 changes. If it doesn't, the code is wrong, not the switch.

docs.title: 3.4 Drift
docs.text: Someone changes the switch by hand (on this fabric it was tested by setting a location string). The next daily plan turns red and names the line. The next apply puts it back.

docs.title: 3.5 Performance and features
docs.text:
From the snapshot: show interfaces counters and counters errors, LACP partners in show linkagg port, show fan, show temperature, show power-supply, show ntp status. The same data feeds the lab's health dashboard.

Think about it

Why does the pipeline never delete a line it doesn't know about, but only report it?

Done when

You can name the four stages of the loop, and say what a red daily plan means.

docs.title: Thank you
docs.text: The read-only client the lab uses is aos_readonly.py (Toolkit T.3). ALE's switches expose the same data through the AOS Web Services REST API described in the AOS 8 Switch Management Guide.

docs.title: Bonus
docs.text: Read the ALLOW list in aos_readonly.py. Which command would you add for a capacity report, and what risk do you check before adding it?

docs.title: Lab S: How this lab was built
docs.text: Version 0.1.0 · draft · 2026-11-18 · class/guides/setup-how-the-lab-is-built.md

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text: Every step of building an HA OmniSwitch Virtual Chassis, in the order it is built. For each one: what was built, how to check it (read-only), how to do it by hand at the console or in WebView, how it is written as code, and where ALE documents it. Read it alongside Labs 1-3. The labs show the result; this page is how you would build it yourself.

docs.title: How the lab is set up
docs.text:
Built by What a one-time console bootstrap (logged, every command kept) factory reset, chassis identity, stack links, management addresses, accounts the lab's network pipeline (plan / apply / read back / daily drift) everything else: system, DNS, NTP, syslog, VLANs, server bonds, checks this demo's pipeline nothing on the live switch: one read-only sign-in and a fixed list of show commands (the snapshot) you read the snapshot; on the sandbox pair (coming soon), build it yourself

The values below are the sandbox example values. The live fabric uses its own, in the lab's network repository. [verify] marks a WebView path or keyword not yet walked on the sandbox. Lab diagram.

Your browser does not play this video.

🎬 Lab S: how this lab was built. Watch it alongside the sections below.

docs.title: S.1 Factory state and the day-0 rule
docs.text:
What was built: a factory switch that pulls nothing from the network or the cloud.

Check: show auto-fabric config → Auto-fabric Status : Disable.

By hand (console, 115200 8N1):

show chassis
show running-directory
auto-fabric admin-state disable          [verify keyword on your release]
cloud-agent admin-state disable

As code: a check that runs after every pipeline run, so a re-enabled Auto-Fabric turns the run red.

Why: zero-touch is a feature, and in a lab whose source of truth is git it is also a risk. A new box must not configure itself from the LAN.

docs.title: S.2 Form the Virtual Chassis
docs.text:
What was built: two chassis, one logical switch. Chassis 1 is the preferred master, and two 100G stack links (VFL) join them.

Check: show virtual-chassis topology (1 Master Running, 2 Slave Running), show virtual-chassis vf-link (both Up), show virtual-chassis consistency (OK, OK).

By hand (each chassis, stack cables UNPLUGGED):

! second chassis only (both ship as chassis 1, so this is the critical line)
virtual-chassis chassis-id 1 configured-chassis-id 2
! preferred master
virtual-chassis chassis-id 1 configured-chassis-priority 200      ! 100 on the second chassis
virtual-chassis auto-vf-link-port 1/1/55
virtual-chassis auto-vf-link-port 1/1/56
! remove any other factory auto-VFL candidate port, so a spare QSFP cannot join the VC
write memory

Then cable 55↔55 and 56↔56, power on chassis 1 first, then chassis 2, then write memory flash-synchro.

As code: the read-back asserts in vc-pair.example.yml (asserts:).

Lessons from the live build: the keyword is configured-chassis-priority, not configured-priority. The two units formed the VC on 55-56 by themselves once the other candidate ports were removed. VC identity lives in vcsetup.cfg; everything else is in vcboot.cfg.

docs.title: S.3 Management plane
docs.text:
What was built: one address per chassis, plus a VC-wide address that follows whichever chassis is master. Automation always targets the VC-wide one.

Check: show ip interface.

By hand:

ip interface local chassis-id 1 emp address 192.0.2.7/24
ip interface local chassis-id 2 emp address 192.0.2.8/24
ip interface master emp address 192.0.2.9/24
ip service http admin-state enable
webview force-ssl enable                 [verify]
ip service telnet admin-state disable
ip service ftp admin-state disable

Lesson: a default route on the management port is refused ("Default routes with gateway on EMP port not allowed"). Use specific static routes.

docs.title: S.4 Accounts and RBAC
docs.text:
What was built: admin (break-glass), automation (the pipeline, with an SSH key), readonly (students and the SME), each with its own password in a vault. No password is ever in code.

Check: show user (as an admin; this command is not in the class's read-only list).

By hand:

user readonly password <from the vault> read-only all

Lesson: the password policy needs at least one digit and one non-alphanumeric character.

Next: sign-in with your Microsoft account through the lab's directory gateway (LDAPS), with your class group mapped to read-only. (Coming soon, proven on the sandbox first.)

docs.title: S.5 VLANs
docs.text:
Check: show vlan.

By hand: WebView Layer 2 → VLAN → Add [verify], or vlan 50 admin-state enable name "compute-50".

As code: vlans: in vc-pair.example.yml.

Lesson: the switch prints ranges (vlan 70-72 …) and the code lists each VLAN. The first live apply's read-back caught that mismatch and saved nothing.

docs.title: S.6 LACP across both chassis
docs.text:
What was built: each server bond has one port on each chassis, so a whole chassis can fail and every server keeps a link.

Check: show linkagg, show linkagg port.

By hand:

linkagg lacp agg 1 size 2 admin-state disable name "server01-bond0" actor admin-key 1
linkagg lacp port 1/1/1 actor admin-key 1
linkagg lacp port 2/1/1 actor admin-key 1
vlan 50 members linkagg 1 tagged
linkagg lacp agg 1 admin-state enable

As code: linkaggs: in vc-pair.example.yml.

Lesson: bond ids above 127 are refused on this model, so the lab renumbered its bonds in code, once.

docs.title: S.7 Save, certify, roll back
docs.text:
Check: show running-directory, show configuration status.

By hand: write memory flash-synchro (both chassis), copy running certified.

As code: saved only after the read-back passes, and only when the switch is running from WORKING (never over the rollback copy).

Lesson: Running Configuration: SYNCHRONIZED compares the two chassis, not running vs saved. show configuration status answers that.

docs.title: S.8 Drift, every day
docs.text: As code: the daily plan goes red when the switch differs from the code. The next apply sends the one line, reads it back, saves, and the re-plan says 0. See Lab 3 and fabric-as-code.example.yml.

docs.title: Thank you
docs.text: ALE: OmniSwitch 6900 · datasheet (PDF). Virtual Chassis, AAA and the Web Services API are covered in the AOS Release 8 Switch Management Guide and Network Configuration Guide (ALE Business Portal).

docs.title: Toolkit: commands, snapshot and code
docs.text:
Version 0.1.0 · draft · 2026-11-18 · class/guides/toolkit.md

The reference every lab uses. Every file here is also on Downloads.

docs.title: T.1 The read-only command cheat sheet
docs.text: aos-show-cheatsheet.txt: every command used in the labs. Each one only shows something.

docs.title: T.2 Reading a snapshot
docs.text:
Before class, the pipeline saved one text file per command plus an index, snapshot.json:

{ "schemaVersion": "1.0", "taken": "2026-11-18T14:00:00Z",
  "commands": [ { "cmd": "show virtual-chassis topology", "file": "virtual-chassis_topology.txt", "bytes": 512 } ],
  "failed": [] }

failed: [] means every command answered. Account lines, SNMP communities and keys are replaced with <redacted> before anything is saved.

docs.title: T.3 The read-only client: aos_readonly.py
docs.text:
aos_readonly.py is the exact program the lab uses to read the live switch. It can do one thing: sign in, run commands from a fixed allow-list of show commands, sign out. It refuses everything else before anything is sent:

python3 aos_readonly.py selftest                  # offline: proves the allow-list refuses config and the redaction holds
python3 aos_readonly.py probe    --host <switch> --user <read-only user> --password-file <file>
python3 aos_readonly.py snapshot --host <switch> --user <read-only user> --password-file <file> --out ./snapshot

It talks to the switch's AOS Web Services REST API: GET /auth/?username=…&password=… to sign in, then GET /?domain=cli&cmd=<show …> with the header Accept: application/vnd.alcatellucentaos+json.

docs.title: T.4 The desired state: vc-pair.example.yml
docs.text: vc-pair.example.yml: an HA pair declared as data (system, DNS, NTP, VLANs, server bonds, and the checks that must pass after every run), in the same shape the lab's network pipeline uses. Example values only.

docs.title: T.5 The pipeline: fabric-as-code.example.yml
docs.text: fabric-as-code.example.yml: a GitHub Actions workflow that plans on every push, applies only when a person dispatches it (behind an approval), and plans for drift every morning.
